ops.title: Release-ordering: daemonkit's next release must follow synckit v0.39.0 and captain-hook 12.22.5, which drop launchd.RemoveUnmarked
ops.description:
Created 2026-08-30 by the change it constrains. daemonkit `b99c8a1` ("decruft: retire launchd.RemoveUnmarked and its ErrMarked sentinel") is on main and unreleased.

**The gap.** Two consumers removed their calls on `origin/main` but have not cut a release carrying that removal, so their LATEST TAGS still call the deleted symbol:

| consumer | latest tag at the time | tag calls it? | removal commit on main |
|---|---|---|---|
| synckit | v0.38.0 | **yes** — `daemon/install.go:255` | `ed7f568 refactor(daemon): drop the pre-v0.21 legacy LaunchAgent sweep` |
| captain-hook | v12.22.4 | **yes** — `internal/hookd/deployment.go` | `1819788 refactor(hookd): drop the pre-v0.21 legacy LaunchAgent sweep` |

Under Go MVS, anything resolving synckit v0.38.0 or captain-hook v12.22.4 together with a daemonkit that no longer exports `RemoveUnmarked` fails to compile. Releasing daemonkit first breaks both.

**How this surfaced, and the lesson.** The D2 lane's last-caller proof was correct — it read every consumer's `origin/main` and found both clean. What it could not see is that `origin/main` is not what a downstream build resolves; a *tag* is. Separately, a fleet-build run reported

    /tmp/fleet-src-runtime/synckit/daemon/install.go:255:17: undefined: launchd.RemoveUnmarked

which looked at first like the D2 proof having been wrong. It was not: that run read the local `~/Code/synckit` checkout, which was 2 commits behind `origin/main` and still sitting at the v0.38.0 release commit. Both readings were about a tree that legitimately still calls the symbol.

**Gap worth noting in the gate itself:** `scripts/fleet-build.sh` marks a leg `*` when that leg's OWN checkout is off its declared ref, but a *cone peer* that is off-ref carries no such mark — so a stale peer silently changes a leg's verdict with nothing in the output saying so. That is what made this look like a contradiction rather than a stale checkout.

**Status:** synckit v0.39.0 pushed (`ac2520e`, "release: cut 0.39.0"), awaiting CI before tagging. captain-hook 12.22.5 is in flight in the same session.</body>

ops.text: synckit v0.39.0 is tagged and released (contains ed7f568, which drops the legacy sweep)
captain-hook 12.22.5 is tagged and released (contains 1819788, which drops the pre-v0.21 LaunchAgent sweep)
Only then does daemonkit cut the release containing b99c8a1, and a full fleet-build against the released consumer tags is green
